verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI is itself a first-party Python library with a typed agent API, so developers build directly against official code. Its docs cover typed generics, tools, structured output and multiple model providers, and community users report building production agents and integrations on its public API. However, the evidence documents only a single Python framework, not an SDK family, and users note the lower-level APIs are painful, missing for 10: official SDKs in more than one language, explicit SDK reference or versioning documentation, and evidence the lower-level programmatic APIs are as usable as the high-level Agent interface.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Agents are Pydantic AI’s primary interface for interacting with LLMs.
In typing terms, agents are generic in their dependency and output types...your IDE can tell you when you have the right type
The new ImageGenerator gives you a direct API, without an agent run.
Public API is easy to extend.
It does make constructing any given agent very easy, though the lower level APIs are a little painful to use.
